newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes slip lower in modest Friday session.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes slip lower in modest Friday session.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices retreated Friday in a modestly active market, featuring weaker sweet crude differentials amid adequate Gulf supplies.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late in the session at $20.95-21.05 a barrel, around 10-15 cents lower than late Thursday.

NYMEX futures showed July contracts trading around 10 cents weaker at $20.85-95 a barrel, but the cash market holds a rough 15 cents premium to paper due to strong Exchange for Physical (EFPs) values.
July EFPs were heard sold at premiums of 14 cents to the paper contracts, traders said.

Domestic grade parcels were fetching softer bids. Traders said a distressed Saharan Blend cargo on offer at July WTI/Cushing -$1.25 sparked a measure of the easier tone seen for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James.
"It's a light sweet crude and it will end-up getting run somewhere in the Gulf," said a cash trader of the foreign cargo.

Dated Brent values also slid on Friday, with the latest deal losing six cents from the previous price, getting done at July Brent -30 cents. The weaker June 12-14 Brent cargo followed a deal for a June 8-10 loader at July Brent -24 cents.
A pair of Brent cargoes were also clocked on Friday.
Late in the session, LLS/St. James talked at 16-12 cents under July WTI/Cushing and Midland/WTI around the last deal at a 36 cents discount.
Traders said confirmed traders were few and far between, with West Texas Sour/Midland sold at WTI/Cushing -$1.57 and Eugene Island at -$1.60.
July Postings Plus business fluctuated between deals at $1.88 and $1.93, talking late at $1.90-93.
Refiners were expected to get more active as next week progressed, traders said.
Outright crude prices were pressured by weakness in the products sector, where June NYMEX contracts expired leading to heavy selling for a wavering unleaded gasoline futures.
